title: Ancient extinct forms should resemble the embryos of their living descendants

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Ancient extinct forms should resemble the embryos of their living descendants

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since embryos partly show the structure of less modified ancient progenitors, ancient and extinct forms should resemble the embryos of their living descendants, though this may be obscured by early-appearing variations and may be undemonstrable because the geological record does not reach back far enough.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we can clearly see why ancient and extinct forms of life should resemble the embryos of their descendants,—our existing species.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “EMBRYOLOGY, laws of, explained by variations not supervening at an early age, and being inherited at a corresponding age”. Scope: extinct ancestors and the embryos of their living descendants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The resemblance prediction can be tested in selected well-sampled lineages. Deep-time preservation and uncertain ancestry make a general test inadequate and potentially confounded by shared primitive traits.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For fossil stem taxa with credible descendant crown groups, compare adult fossil morphology with stage-matched ontogenetic morphologies of living descendants and appropriate adult controls. Excess resemblance to earlier developmental stages supports the prediction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Adult fossils and embryos differ in size, function and preservation.

The oldest relevant forms are sparsely preserved.

Direct ancestor-descendant relationships are rarely identifiable.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.65
data existence: 0.68
data adequacy: 0.38
analysis feasibility: 0.42
discriminating power: 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A morphospace distance from fossils to embryos versus living adults is a concrete criterion, and it can be built for a few skeletal systems that have both fossil scans and developmental series. Most clades lack that joint coverage, and side-branch fossils are an imperfect stand-in for ancestors. The comparison is informative where the landmarks exist and is not a general test across extinct life.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place fossil adults and the embryos and adults of their living relatives in one morphospace and test whether the fossils fall closer to the embryos than to the living adults. The claim is confirmed if stem fossils are repeatedly more embryo-like than their living adult relatives, and refuted if they are as close, or closer, to the living adults across well-sampled clades.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil adults and embryos of descendants are rarely landmarked in the same coordinate system.

A stem fossil is a side branch, so resemblance to an embryo need not mean it preserves the ancestor's adult form.

Early-acting changes, which the claim itself allows, remove the predicted resemblance and make a negative result ambiguous.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.4
